tts.output: pcm_16000 (16 kHz, mono, 16-bit) stored as WAV
tts.disclosure: Test audio synthesised by a non-Meta speech engine (ElevenLabs eleven_v4_turbo, two premade voices). It is clean synthetic speech, not human recordings; results on real speakers may differ.

noise.level: relative to the RMS of samples above 2% of the clean clip's peak
noise.mixed_by: mirror.evaluate.bench_voice.mix_snr (re-mixing reproduces the files byte for byte)

inputs_rule: 72 sentences x 2 voices x {clean, noise15db} = 288 WAV files, listed with sha256 in inputs.json

correction.environment: MIRROR_LLM_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3; recordings served first, live calls only for transcripts never seen before

plan: Each of the 288 files is sent to the speech model once (the client's own transport retry policy applies; every attempt is counted against the budget and recorded in the ledger).
The text baseline (each sentence as text) runs in the same session through the same compiler, recordings and scorer.
WER: word-level edit distance after the frozen normalisation in bench_voice.normalize, corpus WER = total errors / total reference words, per condition and voice.
Operation accuracy: exact match by score_case; audio vs text paired per sentence, voice and condition; exact two-sided McNemar on the discordant pairs.
All rows are reported; nothing is filtered by outcome.
metrics: corpus WER and median sentence WER per condition and voice
exact operation match from audio vs from text (paired), discordant counts, McNemar p
hypotheses: Clean synthetic speech: corpus WER <= 5% and exact operation match from audio within 5 percentage points of the text baseline.
Pink noise at 15 dB SNR: corpus WER <= 10% and exact match within 10 points of the text baseline.
